At that time, the various classes of sentient beings were free from desire, anger, ignorance, stinginess, and envy;
each possessed only a virtuous mind, a mind of loving-kindness, and a mind of peace and happiness, just like parents toward their children or siblings toward one another.

At that time, all sentient beings attained such mental states and conduct; they were filled with peace, joy, and exultation throughout their faculties, and were no longer subject to cold or heat, nor to sorrow or grief.
Thus, all sentient beings were endowed with joyful hearts and did not hear any loud or clamorous sounds.

Furthermore, this great earth was as level as the palm of a hand and composed of lapis lazuli; it produced various deep and vast, wondrous ponds, with steps made of the seven treasures and bottoms strewn with golden sand, filled to the brim with the pure water of eight virtues.

Within those various ponds, immeasurable lotus flowers spontaneously appeared, as large as chariot wheels; these exquisite flowers possessed the colors of the seven precious gems, blooming with subtle beauty, their petals soft and supple. Furthermore, immeasurable lotus flowers were manifested, each one yojana in breadth, variegated in color, exquisite, fragrant, and as soft as kālinga cloth.

Furthermore, he further manifested hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of various lotus flowers as adornments; or he manifested immeasurable lotus flowers two yojanas wide, or three, four, five, up to ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, and even a hundred yojanas wide; or he further manifested immeasurable lotus flowers a thousand yojanas wide.

At that time, a great rain of fragrance fell upon the Sahā Buddha-field, sprinkling and scattering over the ground; the scent of that water was soft and subtle, causing all sentient beings to rejoice and leap for joy.

Various subtle winds blew, causing a rain of diverse, exquisite celestial flowers to fall spontaneously—namely, māndārava flowers, mahāmāndārava flowers, mañjūṣaka flowers, mahāmañjūṣaka flowers, moon flowers, great moon flowers, mind flowers, and great mind flowers—and it rained down such vast varieties of flowers as these.

Furthermore, there were rains of various exquisite powdered incenses; additionally, there appeared fragrant smoke from aloeswood, tagara, black aloeswood, and gośīrṣa sandalwood, which filled every place.

Furthermore, there appeared great wish-fulfilling trees, numbering more than immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of asamkhyeyas, composed of the seven precious jewels. Measuring one yojana up to a hundred yojanas in length, breadth, and height, they were most supremely magnificent and beautiful to behold.

Those various jewel trees were adorned with canopies of various precious garments, silks, white fly-whisks, tassels, and networks of bells; from those jewel trees rained down various exquisite seven treasures—namely, gold, silver, lapis lazuli, mani-jewels, pearls, musaragalva, agate, and strings of red pearls—and such things as these rained down.
Furthermore, from the various jewel trees there fell rains of diverse, supple, and multicolored garments—namely, *kośa* cloth, *kuśa* cloth, *kauśeya* silk, *gośīrṣaka* cloth, and so forth.

Furthermore, from the various jewel-trees there rained down all manner of necklaces, fashioned from Jāmbūnada gold and interspersed with various exquisite and miscellaneous gems—namely, rings, bracelets, earrings, celestial crowns, armlets, seals, pearl strings, precious necklaces, golden chains, and other such ornaments.

Furthermore, beneath those various wish-fulfilling jewel trees, hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of lion thrones appeared, each fashioned from various kinds of the seven treasures. Those lion thrones were seven cubits high; the Bodhisattvas sat upon them, their bodies adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, their countenances upright and majestic, pleasing for all to behold, and their bodies naturally translucent both within and without.

Before all those bodhisattvas, hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of couches appeared, each fashioned from the seven precious gems. Upon each of these couches sat a thousand devaputras, who performed music with the five instruments and sang hymns of praise. Their voices were exquisite and refined, causing the hearts and minds of those who heard them to leap with joy. From within those sounds, various songs of praise emerged, and they spoke these verses:
“Equal and peerless, I possess nothing at all;
Adorned with the perfection of merit, He is a rarity in all the worlds.”
Through the diligent practice of various austerities, this Dharma arises;
through subtle and magnificent deeds, it manifests throughout all worlds.
Capable of removing [suffering] in the hells and other realms, this Dharma arises in such a way.
Adorned with subtle and wondrous phenomena, he thus manifests throughout all worlds.
He is able to eliminate the sufferings of all rebirth paths, such as those of the hells, as well as the sufferings of the various realms of existence; at that time, they are all extinguished.
Having removed those defilements and impurities, as well as the stains of delusion from all people,
and because of these excellent, supreme, and subtle matters, he has appeared among humanity.
Now, in these boundless lands, at this time, they are all level and vast.
The great mountains and all the rivers, Sumeru and the oceans, are all gone;
the ground is made of lapis lazuli, pure and level as the palm of a hand.
Trees of various jewels and colors are exquisite and bring universal joy to behold.
Within this land there are further such things:
Pure and majestic, with flaming radiance, Exquisite golden forms that eclipse the sun and moon.
There are various seats made of diverse jewels, Upon which bodhisattvas sit.
His majestic radiance is like that of a hundred suns, his body adorned with all the marks of excellence.
Beside countless ponds, encircled by mani jewels, the water—
possessing the eightfold virtues— is pure, clear, and full.
Hundreds of thousands of varieties of lotus flowers adorn the ponds;
as vast as chariot wheels, they increase in size progressively.
Furthermore, there are firm seats, composed entirely of precious jewels.
Hundreds of thousands of millions of devas, all celestial hosts of exquisite beauty,
played various subtle and wondrous sounds, offering praise and singing hymns;
through the supernatural power of the Tathāgata, these manifold sublime voices emerged.
From such musical performances, songs, events, verses, and dharmas as these, there are more than immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) dharma-phrases.

At that time, within the assembly of the World-Honored One, all the devas and humans—including those who practice the Mahāyāna, those who delight in the Mahāyāna, and those who believe in the vast mind—by virtue of the power of this boundless radiance, beheld all those Buddha-fields thus adorned with merit and pure.
Among those gods and humans, there were some who followed the path of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas; they neither saw nor knew of the pure adornments and merits of this buddha-field.

As for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in this field, they had all attained immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable samādhis, dhāraṇīs, supernormal powers, and dharma-phrases. Furthermore, there were great śrāvakas who had entered the samādhi of universal quiescence.
At that time, a lion throne appeared spontaneously, measuring one hundred billion yojanas in length, breadth, and height, made of the seven precious jewels and spread with celestial garments.

At that time, there was a Tathāgata whose body was infinitely vast; he appeared upon the seat, sitting cross-legged, his physical marks and signs of excellence majestic and peerless, manifesting in their full perfection.

There was a great lotus flower, equal in length, breadth, and height at eighty-four thousand yojanas, fashioned from the seven treasures, which appeared before the Buddha; it was surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of lotuses, adorned, blooming, soft, exquisite, and majestic.

Furthermore, there were banners, streamers, and suspended canopies in numbers exceeding immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas, composed of various interspersed precious gems; in the midst of space hung immeasurable and boundless pearls and other jewels as well as various silken fabrics, and further suspended were immeasurable and boundless nets of jeweled bells.
Adorned with such merits as these, they manifested spontaneously within this buddha-field.

Thus, unspeakably immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable unprecedented events appeared within this Sahā buddha-field; furthermore, unspeakable, immeasurable, and innumerable powers of great adornment and supernormal faculties—never before seen and never before heard—manifested within this Sahā world-system as such supreme, most excellent, and rare phenomena.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya immediately gave rise to this thought:
"By what cause and by what condition has this rare, inconceivable, and great matter of adornment appeared within this Buddha-field?"
"The power of his supernormal faculties causes the assembly to leap with joy; I shall now question the Buddha, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, to shatter this doubt.

At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva Mahāsattva rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, placed his right knee upon the lotus flower, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I now have a doubt and wish to ask the Tathāgata; I pray that you will open the net of my doubts.
The Buddha told Maitreya:
"The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha always permits you to ask; if you have any doubts, I shall explain them for you."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, having received the Buddha’s permission, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

By what causes and conditions has this phenomenon occurred, wherein such rare, extraordinary, and joyful dharmas have been manifested within this Sahā buddha-field—namely, the manifestation of supernormal powers, the supreme purity and exquisite adornment of the buddha-field with all its merits, being transparent, stainless, and utterly free from all evil thoughts, even to the point of being beyond description, inexhaustible, and never before heard or seen?”
"Bhagavān!
This assembly of bodhisattvas, seeing such supernatural manifestations for the sake of the Dharma appearing in the world, has all its doubts and perplexities.
Bhagavān!"
"What do you wish to do?
Then, Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva spoke a verse to ask the Buddha:
"What rare thing is this in the world now? O Great World-Honored One, why do you manifest such a sight?"
This dharma is a marvel never before seen; now, regarding this matter, doubt has arisen.
It causes the great earth and the vast oceans to tremble, while some abide in pure worlds, unfurling nets of pure golden light that extinguish all darkness in the world.
There are hundreds of thousands of boundless lotuses, as well as various flowers and wondrous jewel-trees;
there are billions of banners, canopies, silken streamers, along with strings of pearls, bells, and nets.
With immeasurable kinds of light from merit and wisdom, You extinguish all suffering in the evil realms;
World-Honored One, for what purpose do you manifest this sign Within this wondrously pure Sahā Buddha-field?
Having spoken these words, the Buddha addressed Maitreya Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, saying:
“You may sit once more; I shall analyze and explain for you the causes and conditions by which this most rare Dharma appears in the world.”
Maitreya!

To the east, beyond as many Buddha-fields as there are grains of sand in the Ganges multiplied by incalculable numbers, there is a Buddha-field named Pure Light-Wheel Merit-Adorned Jewel-Filament Realm. In that Buddha-field there is a Buddha named Fully Blossomed Subtle and Exquisite Adornment of the Dharma-Domain Wheel Single-Canopy Roar Vairocana-Treasury Tranquil Sovereign King Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently travels about, expounding the essentials of the Dharma.
The world is pure, having eliminated all afflictions such as stinginess, greed, hatred, and ignorance, as well as all evil realms.
Within that buddha-field dwell bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the ten stages.

In that buddha-field, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrāntājñānābhijña, who had attained all the dhyānas, samādhis, abhijñās, and dhāraṇīs of the bodhisattvas and was foremost among them. Holding a palace adorned with all kinds of jewels, he was traveling through the air from that realm, accompanied by more than boundless numbers of bodhisattva mahāsattvas, intending to come here to this Sahā buddha-field.

"By the power of this noble being’s majestic spiritual authority (*vīrya*), he has created a great adornment for this world; through his sovereign supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), he first manifested these things.

When the World-Honored One had finished speaking these words, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña and his retinue immediately appeared within a magnificent wheel of light of great majesty. There were nets of immeasurable billions of rays of light that completely surrounded them as they moved through the air, performing hundreds of thousands of kinds of music and songs, while from each division there fell a rain of various celestial flowers.

Furthermore, he emitted hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of light rays that came to this Sahā buddha-field, and immediately established the Palace Adorned with Jewels in the space between the desire and form realms.

Having thus established [the seat], he descended from the air with his retinue to where the Buddha was; joining his palms toward the Buddha, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet and circumambulated him three times.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradharani-vaśitājñānābhijña, together with his retinue, joined their palms in reverence and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We only pray that the Tathāgata, out of compassion for us, will graciously accept this Palace of Jewel Adornments.
Within this Palace of Jewel Adornments, may the World-Honored One preach the peerless, profound, and wondrous Dharma for the great assembly of bodhisattvas.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña, saying:
“Excellent, excellent!
O virtuous man!”
"You now offer this jewel-adorned palace to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha. O noble son!

From Vipaśyin Buddha at the beginning of this Bhadrakalpa, up until the thousand Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa, you have offered this entire jewel-adorned palace in the past, you offer it in the present, and you shall offer it in the future."
“Excellent, O Great Being!
You are indeed able to adorn this Sahā Buddha-field within with such great jewels.
At that time, the Dragon King Sāgara addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Where is the Palace of Jewel Adornment now located?
Furthermore, what is its size?”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Dragon King, saying:
"Dragon King!
That Palace of Jewel Adornment is situated in the space between the realms of desire and form, with a length and breadth equal to a trichiliocosm."
"O Dragon King!

That Palace of Jewel Adornments emerges from the power of the supernatural penetrations and samādhis of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; it is a place of peace and happiness for all Bodhisattvas, worthy of being offered as an act of worship to the Tathāgata."
"O Dragon King!

This precious palace where the Buddha dwells has arisen through the power of the Tathāgata’s merit; it can cause the minds of Bodhisattvas to attain purity, illuminate the worlds of the ten directions, and bring joy to the hearts of all sentient beings. It eclipses all the palaces of the devas and is fully endowed with unspeakably infinite adornments, universally proclaiming itself to all Bodhisattvas throughout the ten directions so that they may take full cognizance of it."
"O Dragon King!

That Palace of Jewel Adornment has white lapis lazuli for its upper surface and Jāmbūnada gold for its walls; it has treasure-trove jewels for its battlements, agate-treasure jewels for its parapets, maṇi-jewel treasures for its railings, pure-light jewels for its pillar posts, and universal-light jewels for its carriage. All manner of jewels form its seats, and various miscellaneous jewels in the shape of half-moons, with boundless radiance, cover the palace above. It has eighty-four thousand *koṭi-nayuta* pillars, composed of various colors and exquisite jewels, perfect in their refinement and providing the most supreme offerings worthy of the Tathāgata."
"O Dragon King!

That jewel palace is hung with various treasures, including immeasurable and boundless nets of pearls, silken banners, and golden bells. It stands adorned with upright, wondrous banners and suspended pennants and canopies. The ground is smeared with ox-head sandalwood and perfumed with the finest, most exquisite incense of solid sandalwood and aloeswood. It is decorated with panels of dragon-jewel pearls and flowers interspersed together, and various kinds of flowers are strewn everywhere across the ground."
“O Dragon King!

Upon all the pillars of that Palace of Jewel Adornment, countless thousands of billions of devaputras sit and produce the five celestial musical tones; they sing most wondrous hymns of praise with leaping joy, and from these musical sounds emerge the gateways of illumination for all dharmas.”
"O Dragon King!

That Palace of Jewel Adornments is sustained by a great wind that circulates all around it. Within it are thousands of billions of exquisite ponds made of the seven treasures, with sands of gold for their bottoms, filled to the brim with pure water of eight virtues. In each pond, countless hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of lotuses are in full bloom, adorned with the seven treasures, of wondrous color and perfect form; these lotuses are as large as chariot wheels."
"O Dragon King!

That Palace of Jewel Adornment has a garden of jewel trees, surrounded on all sides by wish-fulfilling trees adorned with various kinds of precious flowers and fruits. It is decorated with hanging nets of bells and strings of pearls, as well as fine silks and layered fabrics. It emits subtle and wondrous fragrances that cause the heart to leap with joy, and is further adorned with various jeweled stupas of exquisite color and perfect form."
"O Dragon King!

Beneath each tree there is a lion throne made of the seven treasures, with celestial kāśika cloth serving as its cushion. Those lion thrones are high, broad, subtle, and exquisitely perfected, being perfectly suited for all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas."
"O Dragon King!
All the Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, including all their necklaces of adornment and rains of flowers, all appear within this Palace of Jewel Adornments."
“O Dragon King!
Such is the magnitude and the manner of abiding of that Palace of Jewel Adornments.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
“O noble sons! In order to fulfill the vow of the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaravaradharagambhīravikrāntābhijña, you all should follow me to the Palace of Jewel Adornments and sit together there.”
At that time, the World-Honored One rose from his seat, surrounded before and behind by an incalculable number of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

At that moment, the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña was on his right side, and the Bodhisattva Maitreya was on his left; they proceeded calmly through the air toward the Ratnavyūha Palace, and having arrived there, [he entered].

At that time, the World-Honored One entered that Hall of Jewel Adornments together with the assembly of bodhisattvas. Within the hall, facing east, was a lion throne of countless yojanas in height, equal in length and breadth.
At that time, the World-Honored One sat upon it.

When the World-Honored One was seated upon the lion throne, that Palace of Jewel Adornments shook in six ways and emitted hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of immeasurable and various great nets of light—namely, blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, purple, and gold. Those sons of gods played celestial music and offered songs of praise; they rained down great celestial flowers, and the burning of celestial incense continued without interruption.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"O noble sons! Each of you should spread out a lotus seat and sit upon it."
After the World-Honored One had given his command, that assembly of bodhisattvas each took their seats upon lotus thrones.
Once the Buddha and the assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas were all seated, [the assembly was complete].
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña reflected thus:
"I shall now make offerings to the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and furthermore, I shall inquire of him regarding the stage of Buddhahood."

Then, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhara-vaśitā-jñānābhijña rose from his seat and, according to his wish, produced various kinds of immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) flowers, perfumes, ointments, powdered incense, flower garlands, robes, banners, pennants, jeweled parasols, music, and songs of praise. He made offerings to the World-Honored One and the assembly of bodhisattvas, honoring, respecting, serving, and providing for them with a sense of rare wonder; having completed these offerings, he stood by.

Furthermore, he brought forth these supreme articles of offering: namely, strings of precious pearls; flowers made of gośīrṣa sandalwood and the seven treasures; and a great jewel named Lion’s Unobstructed Treasury, pure and translucent. Holding these with his hands, he made offerings to the World-Honored One and the assembly of bodhisattvas. For the sake of making offerings, he scattered them over the Tathāgata until they completely covered him. Having scattered them, he prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, circumambulated him a hundred thousand times, and with palms joined toward the Buddha, praised him in verse:
“Your body manifests immeasurable, wondrous marks; It is level, upright, dignified, and without deficiency.
The shell-like topknot has the color of a peacock or a black bee; The forehead is smooth, lustrous, and broad.”
The ūrṇā-kośa opens perfectly like a wondrous flower; The shape of his two eyebrows resembles the new moon.
His nose is high, prominent, and straight, beyond all comparison; His eyes are like the sun shining upon blue lotuses.
The lobes of his ears are as exquisite as the stalks of a plantain tree; His teeth are even, like white kunda flowers.
His tongue is broad and red, attaining supreme flavors; his lips are thick, full, and the color of vermilion.
His wondrous shoulders are large and rounded, appearing without deficiency; his arms hang down like *sāla* trees swaying in the wind.
His fingernails are long, exquisite, and the color of red copper; his fingers are joined by webs like those of a king of geese.
The soles of your feet bear the mark of the exquisite thousand-spoked wheel, all resulting from your former life as a great donor;
your superior form possesses the merit of a lion’s chest, your physical features are majestic, wondrous, and upright;
your waist is like the grip of a bow or a vajra-pestle, and your private organs are concealed as those of a horse.
Thighs and calves are perfectly rounded like an elephant’s trunk; The ankles are symmetrical, firm, and full;
The soles of the feet and palms bear the mark of wheels with webbing like that of a king of geese; His gait is slow and dignified, like the stride of a lion.
The Tathāgata possesses all these marks; Therefore, I prostrate to the King of Merit.
At that time, having finished his praise, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I now have a doubt and wish to question the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
If the Buddha, the World-Honored One, would resolve my inquiry, I would then venture to request his teaching.
After he had spoken these words,
the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhāraṇī-vaśitājñānābhijña,
saying: "O noble son!
"If you now have any doubts, feel free to ask as you please; I shall analyze and explain them for you, so that your mind may be filled with joy.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
“How many stages of Buddhahood are there that cannot be traversed by any bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, or pratyekabuddhas?
Having spoken these words,
the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara-vaśitājñānābhijña, saying:
“Excellent, excellent, O virtuous man!
Since you now desire to cause all bodhisattvas to be able to clearly manifest the benefit, peace, and happiness of the Buddha’s wisdom, you have been able to ask the Tathāgata about this matter.”
"O virtuous man!
Listen attentively and receive this well; reflect upon it thoroughly, and I shall explain it to you in detail.
O virtuous man!"
The Buddha has ten stages which no bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, or others are able to traverse.
What are these ten?

First is the Ground of Profound, Difficult-to-Know, Vast Wisdom, and Virtue; second is the Ground of Inconceivable Radiant Virtue with the Majestic Dignity of Purified Limbs; third is the Ground of the Ocean-Treasury of Auspicious Marks and the Banner of the Good Moon; fourth is the Ground of the Virtue of Wondrous Golden Light and the Spiritual Power of Wisdom; fifth is the Ground of Radiant Virtue with the Majestic Treasury of the Fire-Wheel; sixth is the Ground of the Manifestation of the Flame-Light that is Internally Pure and Stainless like Space; seventh is the Ground of the Luminous Realm of the Vast and Supreme Dharma-Dhātu Treasury; eighth is the Ground of the Most Pure Universal Awakening Wisdom-Treasury, Capable of Purifying the Stainless and Pervasive Unobstructed Wisdom-Penetration; ninth is the Ground of the Illuminating Power of Boundless Hundred-Million Adornments and Dedication; tenth is the Ground of the Wisdom-Ocean Treasury of Vairocana.
"O virtuous man!
These are the names of the ten stages of the Tathāgata; the wisdom of all Buddhas cannot be fully described.
O virtuous man!"
The first stage of the Buddha is so called because all subtle habitual tendencies have been eliminated and because he has attained mastery over all dharmas.
The second stage is so called because he turns the wheel of Dharma and proclaims the profound teachings.
The third stage is so called because it explains the precepts of the śrāvakas and further elucidates the three vehicles.
The fourth stage is so called because it teaches the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates and further subdues the four kinds of māras.
Regarding the fifth stage: it is so called because one subdues all non-Buddhists in accordance with the Dharma, and furthermore, because one subdues arrogance as well as the various assemblies.

Regarding the sixth stage: it is so called because one instructs immeasurable sentient beings in the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*), and furthermore, because one manifests six kinds of great supernormal powers; namely: manifesting the meritorious adornments of boundless pure Buddha-fields; manifesting being surrounded by boundless assemblies of Bodhisattvas; manifesting boundless and vast Buddha-fields; manifesting the essential nature of boundless Buddha-fields; and manifesting within boundless Buddha-fields the descent from Tuṣita, the entry into the womb, and so forth until the extinction of the Dharma, displaying boundless varieties of supernormal powers.
The seventh stage is so called because for all bodhisattvas it truly explains that the seven factors of enlightenment are non-existent and because there is no further attachment.
The eighth stage is so called because one receives the four kinds of predictions of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for all bodhisattvas.
The ninth stage is for the sake of manifesting skillful means to all bodhisattvas.

The tenth stage is for the sake of explaining to all bodhisattvas that all phenomena are non-existent, and further to inform them that all phenomena are originally quiescent and constitute great nirvāṇa.

When the World-Honored One had finished speaking these names of the ten stages of the Tathāgata, immediately this Sahā Buddha-field, as well as unspeakably many Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions, all manifested eighteen kinds of great signs: namely, the earth shook, shook moderately, and shook greatly; it trembled slightly, trembled moderately, and trembled greatly; it quaked slightly, quaked moderately, and quaked greatly; it made a slight sound, a moderate sound, and a great sound; it roared slightly, roared moderately, and roared greatly; it surged slightly, surged moderately, and surged greatly.

These Buddha-fields—some tilting eastward and rising in the west, others tilting westward and rising in the east; some tilting southward and rising in the north, others tilting northward and rising in the south; some sinking in the center and rising at the periphery, others sinking at the periphery and rising in the center—all such Buddha-fields thus rotated and manifested twelve signs.

Yet, among them, not a single sentient being experienced affliction or harm. A great, supreme light was emitted, illuminating all Buddha-fields, extinguishing all darkness in the world and causing universal radiance to prevail.
All Buddha-lands, whether they contained a Buddha or were devoid of one, whether in a state of formation or destruction, were all manifested within this Buddha-field.

In those buddha-fields, great celestial flowers rained down, filling unspeakably unspeakable numbers of buddha-fields throughout the ten directions—namely, *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, *mañjūṣaka* flowers, *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers, *roca* flowers, *mahāroca* flowers, moon flowers, great moon flowers, and canopy-moon flowers—and so forth. Furthermore, all musical instruments within every field resounded spontaneously without being struck; such exceedingly rare wonders as these appeared throughout all those buddha-fields.

All the attendants in those Buddha-fields rose from their seats and each asked the Tathāgata about various rare and marvelous matters; at that time, those Tathāgatas extensively explained them for their sake, resolving the questions they had raised.

At that time, within this Palace of Jewel Adornments, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhara-vaśitā-jñānābhijña and the assembly of all the bodhisattvas sitting together were all struck with wonder and astonishment, exclaiming:
"How marvelous! How extraordinary!"

For what cause and for what reason has the World-Honored One spoken of this profound realm of the Buddha—the sphere of the Tathāgata’s activity which is extremely deep and difficult to know, subtle and secret and difficult to see, a domain not accessible even to all bodhisattvas, let alone to śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas?
Why is this? We have never before heard of such inconceivable realms of the Buddhas as these ten stages of the Tathāgata.
For the sake of this virtuous matter, we have come together in harmony to request that the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, extensively expound upon the Buddha-stages.
The various bodhisattva-mahāsattvas each rose from their seats, joined their palms toward the Buddha, and addressed him in verse, requesting:
"O Most Victorious and Unsurpassed Honored One, In this world, there is no equal to your teaching.
Regarding all the stages of the Buddhas, You have already spoken their names."
We are now struck with wonder, for never before have we heard such a Dharma.
Having heard the names of these lands, our hearts and minds leap with joy,
like a hungry man thinking of fine food, or a thirsty man longing for sweet spring water.
"Thus do I wish to hear; may the Buddha please explain the various stages (*bhūmi*).
Having spoken these words, those bodhisattvas circumambulated the Buddha three times, prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, and each sat upon a lotus seat.

At that time, the World-Honored One, like a lion king, looked around with composed dignity, surveying the ten directions; having surveyed the ten directions, he addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara-vaśitājñānābhijña, saying:
"O virtuous man!"
The various stages of the Tathāgata are profoundly deep and difficult to know; they are bottomless and hard to realize, transcending all literary expressions and verbal discourse. Why is this?
"O virtuous man!
Even the various stages of the śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and others cannot be described, let alone the various stages of the bodhisattvas or the names of the stages of all Tathāgatas and Buddhas."
Then the Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How many stages of the śrāvakas are there?”
The Buddha said:
"O virtuous man! There are ten stages of the śrāvaka."
What are the ten? First, the stage of receiving the three refuges;

second, the stage of faith; third, the stage of faith in the Dharma; fourth, the stage of the internal ordinary person; fifth, the stage of training in faith and precepts; sixth, the stage of the eight persons; seventh, the stage of the srotāpanna; eighth, the stage of the sakṛdāgāmin; ninth, the stage of the anāgāmin; and tenth, the stage of the arhat.
"O noble son! These are called the ten stages of the śrāvakas.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
How many stages of the Pratyekabuddha are there?
The Buddha said:
“Good man! There are ten kinds of pratyekabuddha stages.
What are these ten?

First is the stage of fulfilling past practices; second is the stage of personally awakening to the profound twelve links of dependent origination; third is the stage of fully realizing the four noble truths; fourth is the stage of profound and sharp wisdom; fifth is the stage of the eightfold noble path; sixth is the stage of fully realizing the realm of phenomena, the realm of space, and the realm of sentient beings; seventh is the stage of realizing cessation; eighth is the stage of the six supernormal powers; ninth is the stage of penetrating the secret; and tenth is the stage where habitual tendencies gradually thin out.
"O Good Man! These are called the ten stages of the pratyekabuddha.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradharin again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
Furthermore, how many kinds of bodhisattva stages are there?
The Buddha said:
“O virtuous man!
There are ten stages for Bodhisattvas.
What are these ten?

First is the Stage of Joy; second, the Stage of Freedom from Defilement; third, the Stage of Radiance; fourth, the Stage of Blazing Wisdom; fifth, the Stage Difficult to Conquer; sixth, the Stage of Manifestation; seventh, the Stage of Far-Going; eighth, the Immovable Stage; ninth, the Stage of Excellent Intelligence; and tenth, the Stage of the Dharma Cloud.
"O virtuous man!
These are called the ten stages of the bodhisattva.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
From what do all things of their own respective stages arise?
The Buddha said:
“O Good Man! All stages of one’s own ground arise from the Buddha-ground.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhara again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
Regarding liberation and liberation, what is the difference between them?
The Buddha said:
“Good man! Are river water and ocean water different from one another?
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara replied:
“World-Honored One!
River water and ocean water differ in their breadth and narrowness.
The Buddha said:
"So it is, so it is, O noble son! The liberation of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas is like the water of those rivers; the liberation of the Tathāgata is like the water of the great ocean."
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One,
do all the great and small rivers flow into the ocean?”
The Buddha said: "So it is, so it is,
O noble son!"
It is as you have said. Why is this?
All dharmas—whether the dharmas of śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, bodhisattvas, or the dharmas of all buddhas—all such dharmas without exception flow into the great ocean of the Vairocana-jñāna-garbha.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhara asked again:
“World-Honored One!

We only pray that the World-Honored One will manifest the first stage of Buddhahood; dwelling in that first stage, may you reveal the realm of all Tathāgatas, so that all śrāvakas, pratyekabuddhas, and others may rejoice and leap with joy.”

At that time, the World-Honored One manifested his own buddha-field, named King of Inconceivable Adornments of Various Jewels and Canopies of Boundless Asaṃkhyeya Merits, which extended in length and breadth over as many buddha-fields as there are atoms in hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Ganges-sands of trichiliocosms.
At that time, all the Buddha-fields entered into the inconceivable adornment of the Buddha-field equipped with boundless,
incalculable (*asaṃkhyeya*) jewels and canopies; they were all identical in name, and therein were all the small Sumerus,
middle Sumerus, and great Sumerus, as well as all the Black Mountains, and the small rivers, middle rivers, and great rivers.
All great oceans, mountain forests, valleys, boulders, peaks, and cliffs, as well as places of filth,
salt marshes, and treacherous evils, were entirely eliminated; there were no longer any realms of hell-beings,
animals, or hungry ghosts, nor any devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, or garuḍas.
Kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth were all completely eliminated;
there were no longer any ornaments such as necklaces or the meritorious adornments of former Buddha-fields.

The entire ground of this buddha-field is composed of lapis lazuli, as level as the palm of a hand. Within this buddha-field, there arise the most supreme and subtle ornaments of precious flowers made of great indra-blue vajra. There is an aśoka grove named the King of Bodhi Trees, formed of the seven treasures and possessing various exquisite colors.
This King of Bodhi Trees is as high as worlds as numerous as the atoms within infinite Ganges-sands of Buddha-fields, its height being equal to its width and breadth.

That King of Bodhi Trees has various exquisite jewels for its flowers, leaves, fruits, branches, and twigs; it is adorned with lion-like unimpeded *maṇi* gems and various precious stones, and draped with nets of *vaiḍūrya*, red pearls, and strings of bells made of silken brocades.

From that bodhi tree, flashes of lightning-like flames issued forth, uninterrupted and unceasing; they emitted either golden light, or the light of mani jewels, or the deep blue light of Indra, or crystal light, or the light of sun-jewels, or the light of moon-jewels.

That king of Bodhi trees emits the most exquisite fragrances—namely, aloeswood incense, tagara incense, black aloeswood incense, tamālapatra incense, black sandalwood incense, nāga-sandalwood incense, gośīrṣa sandalwood incense, and so forth—and when these fragrances are emitted, they pervade that entire buddha-field.
That King of Bodhi Trees emitted sounds of song and praise, or rained down showers of jewels throughout all worlds.
Beneath that Bodhi tree, on its eastern side, there arose a great pond formed of the seven precious gems, pure and free from turbidity, named the Mahābodhi Pond King.

Worlds as deep and boundless as the sands of the Ganges, equal in extent to the atoms within a trichiliocosm, were level in their vertical and horizontal dimensions; their floors were strewn with Jambūnada gold sand, and they were completely filled with water possessing the eight virtues.
The four sides of the pond each have four stairways, filled with various jewels and complete with railings made of diverse precious gems.

From the waters of that pond emerges a great lotus flower named "King of the Aspect of the Well-Expanded Bodhi Lotus," composed of the seven treasures; its length and breadth are as vast as the atoms within a trichiliocosm world-system equal in number to the sands of boundless Ganges Rivers, fashioned from the seven treasures.

Furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of immeasurable and boundless precious lotus flowers surrounding it on all sides; their petals were adorned with various wonderful seven-jeweled treasures, soft and fragrant, inspiring love and joy in those who beheld them.

From atop the pedestal of that king of lotuses emerged the Bodhi-chariot-king, named Boundless Jewel Adornment, composed of the seven precious gems; it was as high as world-systems numbering as many as the atoms in three thousand great thousandfold worlds, equal to the sands of an incalculable number of Ganges Rivers, and its length and breadth were exactly equal.

The garments, ornaments, and supreme excellence of that King of the Jewel-Adorned Bodhi-Chariot were the most preeminent and abundant of the high and sublime; compared to all the garments, adornments, and supernormal powers within that Palace of Jewel Adornments, they did not equal even a hundredth part, a thousandth part, or a hundred-thousand-billionth part—just as the light of a firefly is eclipsed in the presence of the sun’s radiance.
In this way, when the Jewel-Adorned Palace appeared before the King of Bodhi-Chariots Adorned with Boundless Jewels, it no longer appeared at all.

Likewise, all those various, immeasurable, and boundless ornaments, necklaces, garments, supernatural adornments, and radiances caused all the light of the sun and moon to be unable to shine, so that they possessed no brilliance.

Compared to that King of Bodhi Chariots, adorned with boundless jewels, there exists no such brilliance, radiance, essence, or illumination as that of all the Śakras, all the Brahmās, or all the Śuddhāvāsa devas.

From within that palanquin emerged the Mahābodhi Lion Throne King, named "Excellently Illuminating Unobstructed Lion Adornment. It was composed of the seven treasures, its radiance and color were peerless, and it was fully endowed with all manner of requisites. It was covered with Kāśika celestial garments and stood as high as worlds equal in number to the atoms of ten billion Ganges Rivers; its length and breadth were exactly equal.

Śākyamuni then sat upon that lion throne and was renamed the Tathāgata Vimalatejaguṇasiṃhacandraprabhavairocanagarbhasphaṭikadhvajasarvavyūhaprabhāsa-lakṣaṇaguṇatejorāśicandrasūryajñānaprabharāja. His great body became perfectly equal in size to as many trichiliocosms as there are atoms in ten billion Ganges-sands of Buddha-fields, with every limb and part fully complete.

He was fully endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man and adorned his body with the eighty minor characteristics; the halo of light from the wheel on the crown of his head graced his head, making it impossible to see its summit. His body was pure, like the reflection of the sun and moon shining upon a mirror.

The body of that Tathāgata is likewise so: it is devoid of flesh, blood, and marrow; it is not produced through the kalala stage resulting from parents, but is born by transformation, pure like Jambūnada gold, pure vaidūrya, and the deep blue luster of Indra-ratna gems.
The body of that Tathāgata is thus pure, devoid of all subtle habitual tendencies (*vāsanā*).

That Buddha, the World-Honored One, is fully endowed with all the marks [of a Great Man]; he is the Teacher of All-Knowledge, the Sovereign of all Dharmas, who has crossed to the other shore of unsurpassed Perfect Enlightenment. Possessing supreme great compassion, he is the greatest among men.

This lion-like man has already attained the exhaustion of outflows; his body is as firm as adamant, a mass of a hundred merits, fully endowed with the ten powers, the four fearlessnesses, and the eighteen unique dharmas. He lets forth the true lion’s roar; his lifespan is immeasurable, and he dwells in a pure buddha-field where the light of his attainment of the Way is spontaneous and natural, surrounded before and behind by an assembly of immeasurable and boundless bodhisattvas.

Those bodhisattvas each possessed their respective physical bodies in full perfection; beneath the jeweled trees, upon lotus palanquins within those ponds, they sat on lion thrones in perfect proportion to their forms.
Each bodhisattva was individually adorned, just as the Tathāgata is fully endowed with his ornaments.
Thus, this buddha-field is adorned and purified by merit; its inhabitants are pure and its assemblies are pure.
The kalpa is named Boundless Adornment Mahākalparāja, and that kalpa is pure.
If one were to attempt to describe this vast buddha-field and the conduct of the Buddha, it would be impossible.
To awaken in such a manner is called the Tathāgata’s dwelling in the first stage of a buddha.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña, saying:
"Good son! Do you see the Tathāgata’s supernormal power of wisdom?"
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña replied:
"I see them, World-Honored One!"
“I see them,
Tathāgata! the Buddha said.
“O virtuous man!
This is the first stage of the Buddha, named ‘Profound, Difficult to Know, Vastly Radiant Wisdom and Virtue.
O virtuous man!”

You should now know that there are Tathāgatas—Ekacchatra-nirghoṣa-rāja-tejo-vibhu, Ratnaguṇaprabhāsa-garbha-guṇakāya-viśuddha, Acalābhaya-prabhāsa, and Ṛddhibala-padmodbhava-guṇatejo-lakṣaṇa-vijaya-hāra-maṇirāja—who are honored by devas and humans in the realm of Sukhāvatī.

Furthermore, there are Tathāgatas such as Amitābha, Padmavikāsana-tārārāja, Nāgendrarāja, and Ratnaguṇa—those who have attained the Way in such pure Buddha-fields as these. Those Tathāgatas have attained the first stage of Buddhahood (*prathamā bhūmi*), and the Tathāgatas exercise such supernatural powers within this stage that they are no different from my own supernatural powers today.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!

If there are Buddhas, Tathāgatas, in lands of the five turbidities who have currently attained the Way or will attain the Way, do those World-Honored Ones currently or will they attain the stage of a Tathāgata?”
The Buddha said,
"O noble son! Those Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who are able to manifest skillful means can attain it."

Why is this? It is because he gives rise to a heart of great compassion for all sentient beings. He sees that sentient beings are confined within the dense forest of the three realms of existence; these beings are shrouded by the net of craving within the darkness of ignorance, believing in impurity, inverted views, and false perspectives. Facing immeasurable sufferings at the brink of the three evil destinies, they transmigrate through the six paths of rebirth with afflictions revolving one after another, having no beginning and being ignorant of their fundamental origin.
Those sentient beings do not know the Buddhas or the Buddha-dharmas, nor the dharmas of the Bodhisattvas, and they do not know the various liberations as they truly are.
O Good Man!
The Buddhas and Bodhisattvas thus know that all those sentient beings undergo manifold sufferings.
O Good Man!

At that time, when a Buddha appears in a world of five corruptions—whether descending from Tuṣita, entering the womb, dwelling in the womb, being born, growing up, enjoying pleasures in the palace, leaving home for ascetic practice, proceeding to the site of enlightenment, subduing Māra, attaining Buddhahood, turning the Great Wheel of Dharma, engaging in debate with various non-Buddhists while subduing the arrogant multitudes according to the Dharma, or even shortening his lifespan to manifest Great Parinirvāṇa—[the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas know this].

After entering nirvana, by the power of samādhi, he manifests his own body and distributes śarīra relics as large as mustard seeds. Gods, nāgas, humans, non-humans, and others give rise to hearts of joy; for the sake of making offerings, they construct immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of reliquaries.
Some may leave the household life within those teachings to practice asceticism, or act as seeds for awakening, crossing to the further shore of the ocean of afflictions and existence.
"O virtuous man!
All Buddhas possess such a dharma, which enables immeasurable and boundless sentient beings to cross over the ocean of afflictions to the other shore."
"O virtuous man!

You should now know that whatever supernatural powers are manifested by the Tathāgata within the world of five turbidities are all produced through the Buddha’s responsive transformations, or through the supernatural powers of various bodhisattvas, or as manifestations brought forth by skillful means."
The Bodhisattva Samantanetra-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
How many kinds of Buddha-bodies are there?”
The Buddha said:
"Good son! Briefly stated, there are three."
"What are these three?
First is the retribution body (*nirmāṇakāya*), second is the response body (*saṃbhogakāya*), and third is the true body (*dharmakāya*).
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradhāraṇī-vaśitājñānābhijña again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
What is called the Reward Body (saṃbhogakāya) of the Tathāgata?
The Buddha said:
“O virtuous man!

If you wish to see the recompense-body of that Buddha, you should know this now: just as you today see me manifesting the pure buddha-fields of all Tathāgatas—those who have attained the Way and those who shall attain it—all such manifestations are the recompense-body.”
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña again asked the Buddha,
“World-Honored One,
what is called the Tathāgata’s response body (nirmāṇakāya)?”
The Buddha said:
"O virtuous man!

It is just as with the Tathāgatas of Today’s Leap, the Tathāgata Terrifier of Māras, and the Tathāgata Great Compassionate Mind—all such Tathāgatas as these who have manifested as Buddhas or shall manifest as Buddhas in this defiled world; the Tathāgatas appear descending from Tuṣita Heaven, and so forth, until they sustain all True Dharma, all Semblance Dharma, and all Final Dharma."
"O Good Man!
You should now know that such transformative manifestations are all the Response Body (nirmāṇakāya).
The Bodhisattva Samudramegha Gambhīradharavikrīḍitābhijña then asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
What is called the Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata?
The Buddha said:
“O virtuous man!

The Tathāgata’s true Dharma-body is without form, without manifestation, without attachment, invisible, ineffable, without abode, without marks, without retribution, without birth or cessation, and beyond all analogy.”
Thus it is, O virtuous man!

The Tathāgata’s body is the ineffable body, the Dharma-body, the Wisdom-body, the peerless body, the body equal to the unequaled, the Vairocana-body, the space-body, the uninterrupted body, the indestructible body, the boundless body, the body of the Truly Realized One, the non-artificial body, and the incomparable body; this is called the True Body.
The Bodhisattva Sāgaravaradharāṇīśvararājajñānābhijña again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
If the true body of all Buddhas is formless, unmanifest, and even ineffable—if it is ineffable—is this not the characteristic of annihilation?”
The Buddha said:
"Good son! What do you think?"
“World-Honored One, can the realm of empty space be interrupted or characterized by marks?
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña replied,
“World-Honored One!”
"World-Honored One, the realm of space cannot be severed and possesses no marks. Why is this so?"
If the realm of space were subject to interruption, that realm of space could not be called unobstructed.
World-Honored One!
The realm of space has no location of characteristics, no location of accumulation, no location of boundaries, no location of form, nor any location of substance.
Therefore, World-Honored One!
That realm of space cannot be severed and does not possess any characteristics.
World-Honored One!
"This realm of empty space pervades all places.
The Buddha said,
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Excellent man!
It is so, it is so. Excellent man!"
The true body of the Tathāgata is neither subject to interruption nor possesses any marks.
Why is this? O virtuous man!
If the true body of the Tathāgata were subject to interruption, there would likewise be no appearance of Buddhas nor the manifestation of boundless powers of supernatural transformation (*ṛddhi*).

If it possessed marks (*lakṣaṇa*), it would have a locus of accumulation and a physical location that could be grasped or seized; consequently, all ordinary beings (*pṛthagjana*) would simultaneously attain Buddhahood at once, and there should be no sequential order according to time.
"O virtuous man!
Therefore, the Tathāgata’s true body is neither subject to severance nor possessed of marks; it exists solely to perform the Buddha-work for all sentient beings."
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña again asked the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
Among the meritorious deeds obtained by making offerings to the Tathāgata’s true body (dharmakāya), reward body (saṃbhogakāya), and response body (nirmāṇakāya), which yields the greatest merit?”
The Buddha said,
“O noble son! If one makes offerings to the body of a single Tathāgata, that is equivalent to making offerings to the bodies of all Buddhas.”
Why is this? O virtuous man!
All lights are able to destroy all darkness and cause everything to become bright; yet this light does not coexist with darkness.

"So it is, so it is, O noble son! If there are those who each make offerings to the body of the Tathāgata, the meritorious karma they create can destroy all this darkness of ignorance, open the path of the light of liberation, and likewise never dwell together with any dark obstructions."
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña addressed the Buddha again, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will manifest the second stage of Buddhahood.”
The Buddha said, “Noble son!
Are you able to see it?”
The Bodhisattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña said:
“World-Honored One!
I now wish to see you by means of signs.”

At that time, the World-Honored One emitted from a single pore a ray of light named "Illumination of Signlessness," which reached as far as unspeakably unspeakable numbers of Buddha-fields, causing all forms therein to be entirely extinguished.
At that time, the World-Honored One asked the entire assembly of bodhisattvas: "What do you see now?
The bodhisattvas replied:
“World-Honored One!
There is nothing at all; I see only light.
The Buddha said:
“O noble sons! What do you perceive this radiance to be like?
The bodhisattvas replied:
“World-Honored One!
I perceive everywhere a single great radiance throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of nayutas of Buddha-fields, as numerous as the atoms of dust in the sands of the Ganges.”
At that time, the World-Honored One withdrew his radiance, and the Buddha-fields remained established as they were before.
Then the World-Honored One addressed the entire assembly of bodhisattvas, saying:
"If the Tathāgata were to speak of the second Buddha-ground, even you all would find it difficult to know or hear of it, let alone behold the Tathāgata’s third ground through to the tenth ground."
"O virtuous beings!

Just as the radiance of the sun and moon brings great benefit to all sentient beings, it is by the power of the sun and moon that sentient beings come to know a day and a half-day, a month and a half-month, even a year and its various divisions of time. Yet, sentient beings are unable to discern or perceive the physical bodies of those suns and moons; you see only the appearance of their circles of light."

In this way, in this manner, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, brings great benefit to all sentient beings through the power of the Tathāgata. He causes those sentient beings to know all phenomena—whether they be sinful or meritorious, worldly or supramundane, with outflows or without outflows—and having known these phenomena, they realize them as they truly are and cross over the wilderness of all existence.

Those sentient beings are unable to discern or perceive the physical marks of the Tathāgata’s recompense body (*vipākakāya*); they can only observe the forms manifested through supernatural powers and transformations.
Therefore, you should know this: the various stages (*bhūmi*) of the Tathāgata transcend all sounds and languages; there is only the name that can be spoken.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīra-dhāraṇī-vaśitā-jñānābhijña addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Who is it that turns back and delivers all those in the evil realms?”
The Buddha said:
“O virtuous man!

If there are those who, having heard this Mahāyāna Sūtra on the Common Nature of the Ten Stages of the Tathāgata—the profound treasury of Vairocana that enters into the wisdom and conduct of all Buddhas—give rise to faith; and having given rise to faith, they accept, uphold, read, recite, and transcribe it; or if they teach others to transcribe it and explain it extensively for others; or even if they merely accept and uphold the name of this sūtra, O virtuous man!”
"All those who were destined to fall into the various evil realms have immediately attained deliverance.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha,
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that has resolved to attain bodhicitta?
The Buddha said,
"O virtuous man!"
"If one is able to receive and uphold such a sutra as this, even to the point of receiving and upholding its name alone.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha,
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is the one who practices the bodhisattva path?
The Buddha said, "O noble son!"
"If there are those who receive and uphold this sutra.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha,
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that swiftly fulfills and completes the six pāramitās?
The Buddha said, "O noble son!"
"It is one who is able to receive and uphold this sutra.
The Bodhisattva then further inquired, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that shall be destined to encounter a Tathāgata?
The Buddha said, "O noble son!"
"If there are those who are able to hear this sutra, they are [such persons].
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha,
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that has encountered the Buddha and received the prediction of enlightenment?
The Buddha said, "O noble son!"
"It is this one who upholds the secret of the Tathāgata.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha,
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that acts as the great caravan leader for all sentient beings?
The Buddha said,
"O noble son!"
"If there is anyone who upholds this secret treasury of the Tathāgata, it is they.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is the son of the Buddha?
The Buddha said,
"O noble man!"
"There are those who are able to believe in this sutra.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that shall attain all the stages of a bodhisattva?
The Buddha said, "O noble son!"
"Is there anyone capable of hearing this sutra?
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that attains all the Buddha-dharmas?
The Buddha said, "O noble son!"
"There is one who is able to make offerings to this Sublime Dharma Radiance.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!"
"Who is it that knows the Dharma of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas yet does not take up their nirvāṇa?
The Buddha said, "O noble son!"
"There is one who is able to receive this treasury of the sublime Dharma.
The Bodhisattva again asked the Buddha:
"World-Honored One!"
"What is the name of this sutra?
How shall we receive and uphold it?
The Buddha said:
“O virtuous man!

This sutra is named ‘The Equality of the Mahāyāna,’ and it is also named ‘The Exposition of the Entry into the Vairocana-Treasury through the Wisdom-Practice of All Buddhas. You should uphold it thus.”
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
"Desiring to awaken to the Buddha’s Bodhi, With unsurpassed and supreme diligence;
Desiring to turn the holy, outflow-free, Inconceivable wheel of the Dharma of wisdom."
If you wish to erect the banner of the Dharma, if you wish to beat the drum of the Dharma,
if you wish to kindle the lamp of the Dharma, if you wish to blow the conch of the Dharma,
if you wish for the illumination of wisdom, and if you wish to extinguish the darkness of ignorance—
Desiring to gather all sentient beings, To establish them in the wisdom of Bodhi;
Desiring to subdue the armies of Māra, And to make offerings to all Buddhas;
Desiring to illuminate all worlds, With supreme, wondrous, and pure [light].
Unstained by any worldly dharmas, desiring to attain untainted wisdom,
practicing deeds to benefit sentient beings, and wishing to be born in a pure land—
[one should] teach, copy, listen to, and uphold such a wondrous jewel of a sutra as this.
"In order to enable [beings] to reach the Buddha-ground, one should read, recite, and proclaim it.

At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sāgaramati-gambhīradharā-vaśitājñānābhijña, together with the entire assembly of bodhisattvas, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
